\section{Exterior trace amplification of the cyclic arithmetic packet}
\label{sec:exterior-trace-amplification}

\textbf{Purpose and result.}
The cyclic sum construction represents every sum of the selected zeta-zero
jets by the original theta source, with its actual least-norm metric.
Its control operator has only one positive and one negative direction.
An exterior power therefore gives a bound on the \emph{sum} of the positive
spectral defects with the same allowance used for a single vector.
For the polynomial consisting exactly of one nonreal quartet
\(1/2\pm\delta\pm i\gamma\), each root of full order \(m\), the exact bound is
\[
2\delta[1+k(m-1)](k+1)
\left\lfloor\frac{(k+1)^2}{4}\right\rfloor
\leq\epsilon_{h,k,N}^{\mathrm{cyc}},
\qquad N\geq[1+k(m-1)](k+1)^2-1.
\]
It grows cubically for simple roots and quartically for repeated roots.
No off-line zero is asserted, and the subcubic arithmetic upper estimate
is not proved here.

The chapter integrates the complete mathematical argument of
\emph{Tau Exterior Trace Amplification} (12 September 2026), with the
upstream rank-two cancellation written out and the block-to-individual
factor comparison proved below. The delivered Theorems 4.1 and 6.1 are
labelled ET.4.1 and ET.6.1 here. Source hashes, independently executed
finite tests and the scope of the separate Lean contribution accompany
the edition. They are not substituted for these written proofs.

All inverses below act on a nonempty packet. For \(h=1\) the polynomial
relation ideal is the whole ring and every positive-depth coefficient
quotient is zero; its supported zero and external absence remain distinct,
while the analytic function \(g=2\xi\) and its mass remain nonzero.

\textbf{Derivation of the inherited rank-two identity.}
On the line \(S=k/2+iu\), multiplication by \(S\) has adjoint
multiplication by \(k-S\). Orthogonality and the leading coefficient one give
\[
Sp_j=p_{j+1}+\beta_jp_j-\frac{\omega_j}{\omega_{j-1}}p_{j-1},
\qquad \Re\beta_j=k/2,
\]
where the last term is absent at \(j=0\).
Indeed all lower coefficients beyond \(j-1\) vanish by the adjoint identity;
pairing with \(p_{j-1}\) gives the displayed negative ratio, and pairing
with \(p_j\) gives the real part of \(\beta_j\). Substitute its remainders
into \(AK+KA^*-kK\). Internal neighbouring terms cancel with their exact
norm ratios, and the diagonal terms cancel \(kK\). The sole surviving pair
is \((b_{N+1}b_N^*+b_Nb_{N+1}^*)/\omega_N\).
Multiplication on both sides by \(G=K^{-1}\) gives the displayed \(W\).
This is the finite Christoffel--Darboux cancellation in the retained
complex coordinate, not a rank claim for the entire relative module.

The minimum formula is checked by its weighted adjoint:
its remainder is \(KG=1\), its squared norm is \(GKG=G\), and its
pairing with every polynomial in the remainder kernel vanishes.
If \(\chi(S)Q(S)=\sum_i h(s_i)Q_i(\mathbf s)\), fixed-order monic
division gives an original primitive by replacing \(F_h\) with \(\phi_*\)
in factor \(i\), applying \(Q_i(D_1,\ldots,D_k)\), and multiplying by
\((-1)^{i-1}\). The tensor differential supplies the second
\((-1)^{i-1}\), so both signs cancel. Applying this to the numerator
of \(D^{(k)}R-RA\) constructs the primitive used later.
The degree-zero action on \(V\) here is \(-x\partial_x\), intertwining
with \(D\) through \(\Theta\).

\subsubsection{Exact connection to the earlier exterior and diagonal chapters}
The map \(I_{k,p}=\eta^{\otimes p}\operatorname{Alt}_p\) is invariant
under permutations \emph{inside} each block of \(k\) individual factors;
it changes sign under exchanging two complete blocks.
For \(k\geq2\), choose a transposition \(T\) inside one block.
It satisfies \(TI_{k,p}=I_{k,p}\).
The ordinary global antisymmetrizer \(E^-_{kp}\) on all \(kp\)
individual factors satisfies \(E^-_{kp}T=-E^-_{kp}\); therefore
\[
E^-_{kp}I_{k,p}=E^-_{kp}TI_{k,p}
=-E^-_{kp}I_{k,p}=0 .
\]
This proves, through their actual common tensor target, why the present
block exterior image is not the earlier packet \(\bigwedge^{kp}E_h\).
Its comparison with the full tensor minimum is precisely the
\(\Delta^*\Delta\) and control identity above, not an identification
with a global alternating minimum.

For \(k=1\), \(C=E_h\), \(\eta=M_{\upsilon_h}\), and
\[
I_{1,p}=M_{\upsilon_h}^{\otimes p}\operatorname{Alt}_p
=\operatorname{Alt}_p\,\bigwedge\nolimits^pM_{\upsilon_h}.
\]
Thus the earlier exterior construction is recovered by the displayed
invertible full-unit map, with its Gram congruence retained.
For \(p=2\), the preceding diagonal chapter applies algebraically with
its monic polynomial replaced by \(\chi\): use block coordinates \(S_1,S_2\),
\(T=S_1+S_2\), \(r=S_1-S_2\), and \(\Delta=r^2\).
Then
\[
\chi(S_1)=H_0(T,\Delta)+rH_1(T,\Delta),\qquad
\chi(S_2)=H_0(T,\Delta)-rH_1(T,\Delta)
\]
gives its same symmetric and alternating quotient maps, with all
\(\chi\)-jets retained. Their source pairing is now the \(k\)-block
pairing \(G\otimes G\), not the earlier two-single-factor pairing.

appendix:
\subsection[\hspace{0.4em}Reading and verification scope]{Reading and verification scope}
The full delivered mathematical argument in Sections 2--10 is retained
above, with presentation headings adapted and the explicit integration
clarifications shown. The original delivery, its manifest and checker
remain unchanged in the source package.
The source-generated minimum and primitive were checked against
\emph{Tau Cyclic Sum Control}, Sections 3--4, rather than inferred from
the delivery summary.

The classical background is attributed to
\href{https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/0613006}{Overton and Womersley,
\emph{On the Sum of the Largest Eigenvalues of a Symmetric Matrix}
(1992), pp.\ 41--45}. Its official abstract identifies the Ky Fan
principle; no full reading of the paywalled article is claimed.
The complete rank-two argument used here is written above.
The tensor differential and permutation signs agree with
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GWN}{Stacks Project,
Tag 0GWN}. The literal factor in \(g=2\xi\) and reflection equation agree
with \href{https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.4}{DLMF 25.4.3--25.4.4}.
The recurrence is the retained-coordinate instance of
\href{https://dlmf.nist.gov/18.2}{DLMF 18.2(iv)--(v)}.

The finite regression examples supplement the written arguments.
They do not evaluate the actual zeta integrals or prove the required
growth bound. The separate conormal-tower Lean work formalizes specified
quotient maps and a combinatorial maximum; it does not turn this analytic
exterior chapter into a Lean certificate.
